ingredients: 24 Fresh Tomales Bay oysters (or other variety)
1/8 cup kanzuri paste (or other Korean chili paste)
method: Set oven to broil on high. Roast the strawberries until charred under the broiler for 10 minutes. Remove from the oven, allow to cool, then finely chop. Combine all ingredients except oysters in a bowl and stir until well incorporated. Cover and set aside in refrigerator to chill while you shuck the oysters. Shuck the oysters flat-side up so the brine remains in the shell. Just before serving, add a teaspoon of mignonette to each oyster and serve on a bed of crushed ice.
storyTitle: Whisky and Oysters Are A Delightful Match

name: Bombo 2
intro: Serves 1
ingredients: 1/4 oz. burnt cinnamon simple syrup (recipe below)
method: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass and top with ice. Stir vigorously for 20 seconds. Strain into a rocks glass over a large cube. Garnish with an orange peel.

subs.name: Burnt Cinnamon Simple Syrup
subs.method: Add cinnamon sticks to a dry sauté pan (cast iron or stainless steel). Bring the pan to medium heat while stirring the sticks with a wooden spoon for 3-5 minutes or until aromatic and darkened to a deep brown, almost black color. Remove from heat. Combine sugar and water in a pot, bring to a boil, and simmer, stirring occasionally, until sugar has completely dissolved. Remove from heat. Add toasted cinnamon sticks to simple syrup, let cool, and transfer to a sealed container. Refrigerate for up to 1 month.

storyTitle: Whisky and Oysters Are A Delightful Match

name: Long House
intro: Serves 1
ingredients: 1/4 oz. burnt cinnamon simple syrup (recipe above)
3 dashes Herbsaint Pineapple fronds and lime wheel for garnish
method: Pour all ingredients in a shaker tin and top with ice. Shake vigorously for 20 seconds. Strain into a tulip glass with pebble ice. Garnish with pineapple fronds and lime wheel.
storyTitle: Whisky and Oysters Are A Delightful Match

name: The Gentlemen
method: Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass. Add ice and stir for about 10 seconds to dilute and chill. Strain over a large cube in a rocks glass. Garnish with orange twist.
storyTitle: A Bright, Floral Old Fashioned

name: Plane M.I.A.
credit: Created by Stephanie De Luna, bar supervisor, JohnMartin’s Irish Pub & Restaurant, Coral Gables, Florida
intro: This velvety cocktail is a bold, zesty mix of spicy bourbon, bittersweet Aperol, and tangy lime, De Luna says. Bitters and star anise add aromatic depth.
ingredients: 2 oz. Virgil Kaine Ginger-Infused bourbon (or other ginger-spiced bourbon)
Dehydrated lemon wheel and star anise for garnish
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for 15 to 20 seconds, then double strain into a chilled coupe. Float lemon wheel and star anise on top as garnish.
storyTitle: Prepare for Takeoff With These Variations on The Paper Plane Cocktail

name: Emergency Exit
credit: Created by Jonathan Parker, bartender, Bank and Bourbon, Philadelphia
intro: Honey liqueur and lemon help smooth out the sharp edges of Cynar and Aperol, while rye-heavy bourbon lends classic fall spice flavors to this cocktail.
ingredients: 1 oz. Stoll & Wolfe Pennsylvania rye (or other rye)
¾ oz. fresh Meyer lemon juice
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for 30 seconds. Strain into a coupe and float dehydrated lemon wheel on top.
storyTitle: Prepare for Takeoff With These Variations on The Paper Plane Cocktail

name: The Pilot
credit: Created by Alyssa Sartor, beverage director, Little Dipper, New York City
intro: “Black tea brings a slightly smoky, nutty flavor to the scotch in this version of the Paper Plane,” Sartor says. “That, combined with the floral yet bitter quality of the Degroff Aperitivo and a touch of honey for sweetness, makes for a great fall drink.”
ingredients: ¾ oz. black tea-infused blended scotch (recipe below)
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for 15 to 20 seconds. Double strain into a coupe and garnish with lemon twist.Black Tea-Infused Blended Scotch Add tea bag to scotch and let sit in the fridge for two hours. Use immediately.
storyTitle: Prepare for Takeoff With These Variations on The Paper Plane Cocktail

name: Sir Pilot Newton
credit: Created by Brendon Jordan, bartender and bar director, The Blue Ox, Boston
intro: “Reduced cider plays wonderfully with the rye notes of the bourbon in this sophisticated cocktail,” Jordan says. Acidic lemon, bitter Aperol, and sweet herbaceous Nonino balance everything out.
ingredients: ¾ oz. Heaven Hill 7 year old bottled in bond (or other bonded bourbon)
½ oz. boiled cider syrup (like Woods Cider Mill)
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for 15 to 20 seconds. Double strain into a chilled martini glass. Express lemon peel over top and discard.
storyTitle: Prepare for Takeoff With These Variations on The Paper Plane Cocktail

name: Aereo Di Carta Old Fashioned
ingredients: 2 oz. WhistlePig 6 year old PiggyBack (or other high-corn bourbon)
Orange peel and Luxardo cherry for garnish
method: In a mixing glass, stir all ingredients together for 20 to 30 seconds. Strain over a large cube in a rocks glass. Garnish with orange peel and Luxardo cherry on a pick.
storyTitle: The Perfect Fireside Cocktail

name: Candy Corn Old Fashioned
credit: Created by Owen Sears, bartender, Virgin Hotels New Orleans
intro: Everyone may love to hate candy corn, but who doesn’t love an Old Fashioned? Here, corn liqueur balances sweet marshmallow syrup, creating a cozy, rich, well-rounded cocktail.
ingredients: 2 1/2 oz. Elijah Craig straight rye (or other rye)
method: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass and fill with ice. Stir for at least 10 seconds, then strain into a rocks glass and garnish with orange twist.
storyTitle: Trick-or-Treat Cocktails For The Grown-Ups to Celebrate Halloween

name: Peanut Butter Cup
credit: Created by Devin Kennedy, partner and creative director, Press Club, Washington, D.C.
intro: “This is like getting a full-sized Reese's while trick-or-treating,” Kennedy says.
ingredients: 1 1/2 oz. peanut butter fat-washed whiskey (recipe below)
method: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass and fill with ice. Stir for 15 to 20 seconds. Strain over a large cube in a rocks glass.

subs.name: Peanut Butter Fat-Washed Whiskey
ingredients: 750 ml. Rieger’s Kansas City Whiskey (or any rye or bourbon)
subs.method: Spread peanut butter across a large baking sheet with a lip, creating a thin, even layer. Pour whiskey over top. Cover the sheet tightly with plastic wrap to prevent evaporation and allow to sit overnight at room temperature. The next day, strain the whisky through a coffee filter and funnel it back into the bottle. Discard the peanut butter. Keep refrigerated for two to three weeks.

storyTitle: Trick-or-Treat Cocktails For The Grown-Ups to Celebrate Halloween

name: Halloween Crutch
credit: Created by Nicole Morais, director of food and beverage, Grande Lakes Orlando
intro: “This combination of spice and bourbon was inspired by classic Halloween flavors, like caramel apples and spiced sweets, making it the ideal drink for any festive gathering,” Morais says.
ingredients: 2 oz. Contradiction bourbon (or other four-grain bourbon)
Maraschino cherry and orange twist for garnish
method: In a mixing glass, add sugar cube and orange bitters. Muddle until sugar cube is dissolved. Add ice, then pour in bourbon, Pimento Dram, and apple cider. Stir until well chilled, about 10 seconds. Strain into a rocks glass over a large cube. Garnish with cherry and orange twist.
storyTitle: Trick-or-Treat Cocktails For The Grown-Ups to Celebrate Halloween

name: Harvest Moon
credit: Created by Mickey Mullins, beverage director, The Bower and Bower Bar, New Orleans
intro: This drink starts with bright red apple and fall spice, with a slight burn of rye at the finish. The aquafaba gives the drink a luxurious texture reminiscent of a caramel apple.
ingredients: 3/4 oz. 360 Red Delicious Apple Flavored vodka
1/2 oz. Reàl pumpkin puree (or other pumpkin puree syrup)
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for 30 seconds. Strain over ice in a rocks glass and garnish with lemon slices.
storyTitle: Trick-or-Treat Cocktails For The Grown-Ups to Celebrate Halloween

name: After Life
credit: Created by Jenna Marmaduke, bartender, Sonder Social Club, Dunedin, Florida
intro: Elevate classic fall flavors into something richer and more complex. “The bourbon brings warmth, like a fire on a crisp autumn night, while the chai spices and hint of pumpkin evoke the flavors of the season,” Marmaduke says. “It’s like a grown-up version of all the treats we loved as kids, but with a sophisticated, festive twist.”
ingredients: 1 1/2 oz. Angel’s Envy (or other port-finished bourbon)
1/2 oz. Giffard Piment d'Espelette (or other chile liqueur)
1/2 oz. Reàl pumpkin puree (or other pumpkin puree syrup)
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for 30 seconds. Strain over crushed ice in a skull glass or highball. Garnish with cinnamon stick.

subs.name: Vanilla Chai Syrup
subs.method: Bring water to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Add tea bags, remove from heat, and let steep 30 minutes to 1 hour (the longer, the stronger the flavor). Remove tea bags and return pot to the stove over medium heat. Add sugar, stirring until dissolved, about 1 to 2 minutes. Strain into a sealable container. Keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.

storyTitle: Trick-or-Treat Cocktails For The Grown-Ups to Celebrate Halloween

name: White Chocolate and Corn Sheet Cake with Honey Whiskey Glaze
ingredients: 6 oz. high-quality white chocolate baking bar, such as Ghirardelli, Valrhona, or Guittard
1 cup Bob’s Red Mill corn flour
storyTitle: Whiskeys Made from Heirloom Corn Pair Perfectly With This Texas Dessert

name: PSL Martini
ingredients: 1 oz. Green River 1885 (or any straight bourbon)
1 oz. Gosling's Black Seal (or other black rum)
thin orange slice and 3 espresso or coffee beans for garnish
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin. Add cubed ice and hard shake for 20 seconds until the shaker is cold to the touch and has some condensation. Strain through fine mesh into a martini glass. Garnish with orange slice and espresso beans.

subs.name: Pumpkin Spice Syrup
subs.method: Add puree, sugar, and water to a stainless-steel pot. Bring to a mild simmer over medium-low heat. Simmer for 5 minutes until thickened, stirring regularly to prevent the puree from sticking to the bottom. Remove from heat and strain through a fine mesh strainer. Rinse the pot, place over low heat, and add the sweetened condensed milk. Once warm, slowly stir in the pumpkin syrup. Stir over low heat for three to four minutes without letting simmer. Remove from heat and add vanilla and pumpkin pie extracts. Pour into a sealable container. Keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.

storyTitle: A Cocktail Created For Whisky Fans Who Love Pumpkin Spice

name: Brownstoner
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin filled with ice. Stir for about 30 seconds, then strain into a martini glass. Twist orange peel over glass to release oils, then add peel to glass for garnish.

subs.name: Nutmeg-Infused Bourbon
subs.method: Place nutmeg in a clean two-quart mason jar or glass bottle and add bourbon. Cover tightly and store in a cool, dark place. Taste each day until infusion reaches desired intensity, about five days. (If it’s too intense, dilute it to taste with additional plain bourbon.) Strain through a fine-mesh strainer or cheesecloth into a clean jar or bottle. Store refrigerated for up to 3 months.

storyTitle: A Nutmeg-Infused Bourbon Takes This Manhattan to New Heights

name: Star Gazer
ingredients: 1 1/4 oz. High N’ Wicked (or other rye whiskey)
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for about 15 seconds or until the shaker is cold to the touch and frosty. Double strain into a coupe. Garnish with lemon twist.
storyTitle: A Spicy Rye Cocktail That's Perfect For Fall Sipping

name: Jewel Box
ingredients: 1 oz. Elijah Craig Small Batch (or other bourbon)
1 mint sprig and freshly grated nutmeg for garnish
method: Add all ingredients to a julep cup and briefly muddle very gently. Fill cup with crushed ice. Garnish with mint sprig and grated nutmeg.

subs.name: Demerara Syrup
subs.method: Combine sugar and water in a pot over low heat. Stir until sugar dissolves completely, about 15 to 20 minutes. Let syrup cool, then transfer to a sealable container. Keep refrigerated for up to 1 month.

storyTitle: A Bubbly Cocktail to Toast the End of Summer

name: Partly Cloudy Skye
ingredients: 1 1/2 oz. Torabhaig Allt Gleann (or other single malt scotch)
1 1/2 oz. Taylor Fladgate Chip Dry (or other white port)
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin. Dry shake for 45 to 60 seconds. Strain over ice in a highball. Garnish with a lemon twist.
storyTitle: This Cocktail Tastes Like Beach Time In a Glass

name: Southern Charm Hot Brown
credit: Serves 4
ingredients: 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved or whole
method: Preheat oven to 350°F. Season turkey breast with salt, pepper, and garlic powder to taste. Roast, covered, in a roasting pan, until it reaches an internal temperature of 158°F, approximately 30-40 minutes. Remove from oven, keep covered, and allow to rest for 15 minutes. It will continue cooking from its own heat, and should reach an internal temperature of 165°F. Slice. Note: You can opt for store-bought roast turkey from the deli, but roasting it yourself is preferable. Toast slices of artisanal bread to provide a sturdy foundation for the open-face sandwich. Place 2 slices on each of 4 plates. Layer approximately 1/8 lb. of roasted turkey on top of the toasted bread. Generously drizzle the truffle-infused mornay sauce over the turkey. Place one prosciutto crisp atop each open-face sandwich. Scatter cherry tomatoes on top. Sprinkle with chives and parsley. Heat béchamel in a pot over medium-low heat until it begins to bubble. Add finely grated gruyère cheese and truffle oil. Stir until smooth and velvety. Set aside. Lightly spray a cookie tray or line with a silicone mat. Place prosciutto in a single layer on the tray. Bake at 350°F for about 15 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Set aside.
storyTitle: Try This Twist On The Kentucky Classic Hot Brown

name: Peppered New York Sour
credit: Frances Leary, beverage curator and general manager of Down One Bourbon Bar & Restaurant, Louisville
intro: “This cocktail has a savory finish from the red wine to complement the Hot Brown,” explains Leary. “However, it also provides delightful contrast with the fresh acidity that the lemon provides,” which cuts through the richness of the dish.
ingredients: 2 oz. black peppercorn-infused Four Roses Small Batch (recipe below)
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker, except wine, fill with ice, and shake until well combined. Strain over fresh ice into a rocks glass. Use a spoon to float cabernet sauvignon. Toast 1 cup of black pepper-corns in a thoroughly warmed pan for 1 to 3 minutes, or until fragrant. Let cool, then add to one 750 ml bottle of bourbon. Let sit for 24 hours, then strain out the peppercorns.
storyTitle: Try This Twist On The Kentucky Classic Hot Brown

name: Poached Whiskey Peaches With Vanilla and Pink Peppercorn
intro: Sweet, sappy peaches become summer’s elegant post-dinner darling when gently poached in liquid gold composed of vanilla, peppercorns, and whiskey. A modestly priced rye whiskey such as Rittenhouse or a rye-heavy bourbon, like Old Forester 100 or Wild Turkey 101 add a pleasant spice to fragrant fruit-leaning pink peppercorns. Leftover peaches stored in the poaching liquid can be magnificently versa
ingredients: 4 semi-firm ripe peaches, halved and pitted
method: Combine all ingredients, except the peaches, in a large pot and bring to a boil. Stir occasionally. Boil for two minutes until the sugar has dissolved. Turn the heat down to a simmer. Add the peaches and cook, skin side up for about 5-7 minutes if firm, and about 4 minutes if soft and ripe. Turn the peaches over and cook for an additional 5 minutes or until tender when poked with a fork. Remove the peaches with a slotted spoon to a shallow bowl or curved plate. Set aside to cool. Without puncturing the peaches, gently peel skins off once cool enough to handle. Bring the liquid mixture to a boil and cook for 12-15 minutes, until thickened and syrupy. Serve the peaches with a spoonful of the poaching syrup, slightly warm or at room temperature. Can be served with a drizzle of heavy cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream (optional). Store peaches in their syrup, tightly covered, in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. TIP: Use leftover syrup in place of raw sugar in an Old Fashioned.
storyTitle: 3 Easy Whiskey-Infused Desserts Perfect for Summer

name: Blackberry Trifle with Rosemary Cream and Pine Nut Crumble
intro: Take advantage of summer fruit’s juiciest and richest candy-like star—blackberries. The berries are stewed with bourbon into a quick compote, imbuing a grape-like sweetness beside a woody rosemary whipped cream and pine nut crumble. Another healthy dose of bourbon is brushed over the dessert’s anchor, pound cake, which when purchased from the store makes for a swift assembly. A dark-fruit forward
ingredients: 1 store-bought pound cake, or homemade, cut into 1/4-inch slices
3 ½ cups fresh blackberries, plus more for topping
6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, room temperature and cubed
¼ cup pine nuts, lightly chopped
method: Heat cream and rosemary over medium heat until it just reaches a simmer. Remove from heat, cover, and let infuse for 20 minutes. Tightly cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours. Can be made up to 3 days in advance. To make the compote, stir 2 cups of blackberries, 1/3 cup bourbon, and ½ cup brown sugar over medium heat, cooking for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until jammy. Set aside to cool. To make the crumble, combine butter, pine nuts, flour, and ½ cup sugar in a bowl. Spread onto an even layer baking tray lined with parchment and bake until golden brown, about 18-20 minutes. Cool completely. With a whisk or in an electric mixer with the whisk attachment, beat the rosemary-infused cream on high until soft peaks form. Be careful not to over whip. Toss the remaining 1 ½ cups of blackberries with orange zest and ¼ cup brown sugar immediately before assembling.
storyTitle: 3 Easy Whiskey-Infused Desserts Perfect for Summer

name: Espresso, Irish Cream & Coconut Ice Pops
intro: If you’re stuffed full of summer fruit and the idea of another 4:00 p.m. iced latte is sounding repetitive and downright lackluster, this cool concoction of espresso, Irish cream liqueur, and coconut creates ice pops that are a refreshing pick-me-up. A fun play on an adult favorite with a tropical twist, these frozen treats are creamy and rich without being too heavy. Baileys is what you’ll likely
ingredients: ¼ cup + 2 Tbsp. sweetened condensed coconut milk
method: Bring the water to a boil, add instant espresso. Stir until dissolved. Remove from heat and cool to room temperature. Combine ¾ cup of coffee, ¼ cup sweetened condensed coconut milk, heavy cream, and salt. Pour evenly into 8 ice pop molds. Place in the freezer for 1 hour. Remove from freezer and insert ice pop sticks. Return to freezer. Stir to combine 2 Tbsp. sweetened condensed coconut milk, 1/3 cup Irish cream, ¼ cup shredded coconut, and ¼ cup of coffee in a small bowl. Remove ice pops from the freezer and pour evenly over each of the frozen pops. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and return to the freezer for at least 4 hours or overnight. To release the ice pops run the bottom of the molds under hot water. Garnish with shredded coconut and serve. Store in the freezer for up to 6 months. TIP: You can use strong coffee in place of the espresso. Aim to use a dark-roasted brew as opposed to fruity and acidic light-roasted coffee.
storyTitle: 3 Easy Whiskey-Infused Desserts Perfect for Summer

name: Smokey Apothecary
ingredients: 1 1/2 oz. Buffalo Trace bourbon (or other bourbon)
1/2 oz. float Port Charlotte 10 year old (or other peated Islay scotch)
Dehydrated lemon wheel, candied ginger, and edible flower for garnish
method: Add bourbon, ginger liqueur, lemon juice, and strawberry syrup to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for about 3 seconds. Strain over pebble ice in a rocks glass. Float scotch on top and garnish with dehydrated lemon wheel, candied ginger, and edible flower.

subs.name: Strawberry Syrup
subs.method: Combine ingredients in a pot. Muddle strawberries, then bring to a low boil over medium heat. Stir until sugar is dissolved. Then let the mixture simmer for about 10 minutes. Remove from heat to cool. Strain into a squeeze bottle or a sealable container. Keep refrigerated for two months.

storyTitle: This Summery Penicillin Is Just What the Doctor Ordered

name: AMERICAN SINGLE MALT
credit: Maddie Kaye, retail and spirits assistant for Bern’s Co., Tampa
ingredients: 1½ oz. Bulleit American single malt (or other domestic single malt)
3 dashes Fee Brothers Fee Foam Sea salt, cracked black peppercorn, and ground espelette pepper
method: Dry shake all ingredients, then add ice and shake vigorously. Double strain into a coupe. Sprinkle a mixture of sea salt, cracked black peppercorn, and ground espelette pepper on top of the drink, and garnish with dehydrated baby corn. Slice kernels off one corncob and boil them in water with a pinch of salt for 15 minutes or until tender. Strain the kernels and blend in a blender until smooth.
storyTitle: Summertime Sippers

name: BOURBON
credit: Zack Staten, bartender at Barn8 Restaurant + Bourbon Bar, Goshen, Ky.
ingredients: 1½ oz. Old Forester 100 proof (or other high-proof bourbon)
¾ oz. ginger and thyme syrup (recipe below)
½ oz. fresh purple beet juice
method: Shake all ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled rocks glass. Garnish with candied ginger. Make a simple syrup (1:1 sugar and water). Peel and chop a small bulb of ginger for every pint of simple syrup. Blend the ginger and simple syrup until smooth. For one pint of syrup, add 20 sprigs of lemon thyme and let infuse for 2 hours. Strain thoroughly and store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 1 month.
storyTitle: Summertime Sippers

name: CANADIAN
credit: Jay Cullen, bar manager at Long-man & Eagle, Chicago
ingredients: 1 oz. Lot No. 40 (or other rye-heavy Canadian)
¾ oz. Pierre Ferrand Dry Curaçao
method: Shake all ingredients with ice and double strain into a coupe. Express a lemon peel over the drink and then use it as garnish.
storyTitle: Summertime Sippers

name: IRISH BLEND
credit: Mike Herchuck, director of operations for Florida-based American Social Bar & Kitchen
ingredients: 1 oz. Proper No. Twelve (or other blended Irish)
½ oz. RumHaven Coconut rum liqueur
Mint sprig and dehydrated pineapple slice for garnish
method: Shake all ingredients with ice. Strain into an ice-filled tiki or Collins glass. Garnish with a mint sprig and dehydrated pineapple slice, then float Kraken on top. In a small saucepan combine 3 cinnamon sticks (each broken into bits), ¼ cup star anise pods, 2 tablespoons fennel seed, 2 tablespoons Szechuan peppercorns, and 1½ teaspoons whole cloves. Heat for 2-3 minutes until you detect a spiced fragrance. Add 2 cups water, ¼ cup sugar, and 2 Tbsp. honey, simmer for 5-6 minutes on medium heat, stirring to melt the sugar and honey. Turn off heat and allow to steep for 2-3 hours. Strain thoroughly and store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 1 month.
storyTitle: Summertime Sippers

name: IRISH SINGLE MALT
credit: Ian Alexander, bar director at The Dead Rabbit, New York City
ingredients: 1½ oz. Teeling single malt (or other Irish single malt)
method: Shake all ingredients with ice and strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube. Garnish with a cucumber slice.
storyTitle: Summertime Sippers

name: JAPANESE
credit: Jeff Sinanaj, beverage director and co-owner of Empire Steak House, New York City and Tokyo
ingredients: 1 oz. Yamazaki single malt (or other Japanese single malt)
Blood orange slice and rosemary sprig for garnish
method: Shake all ingredients with ice and strain into a rocks glass over a big ice cube. Garnish with a blood orange slice and rosemary sprig.
storyTitle: Summertime Sippers

name: RYE
credit: John Maraffa, corporate beverage manager for Morton’s The Steakhouse
ingredients: 2 oz. Rabbit Hole Boxergrail (or other rye)
3 mint leaves, plus a sprig for garnish
method: Shake all ingredients with ice until shaker is frosted and strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube. Garnish with a mint sprig.
storyTitle: Summertime Sippers

name: SCOTCH BLEND
credit: Nicole Ruwell, bartender at Prezzo, Boca Raton
ingredients: 2 oz. Johnnie Walker Black (or other blended scotch)
3-4 large fresh basil leaves, plus a sprig for garnish
method: In a cocktail shaker, muddle 3-4 basil leaves. Add remaining ingredients and ice and shake. Strain into a rocks glass over a big ice cube and garnish with a basil sprig.
storyTitle: Summertime Sippers

name: SCOTCH SINGLE MALT
credit: Jeff Knott, owner, and Eron Plevan, head bartender at Tartan House, Louisville
ingredients: 1½ oz. Ledaig 10 year old (or other smoky scotch single malt)
1 oz. Giffard Abricot du Roussillon apricot liqueur
method: Shake all ingredients (except soda water) with ice and strain into a Collins glass. Stir in soda water. Combine 1 cup fresh ginger juice with ¾ cup sugar over low heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Strain and let cool, then store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 1 month.
storyTitle: Summertime Sippers

name: WORLD WHISKY
credit: Steven Marshall, lead bartender at Dirty Habit at Hotel Zelos, San Francisco
ingredients: 1¾ oz. Kavalan Classic (or other Asian single malt)
½ oz. honey syrup (1:1 honey and water)
¾ oz. fresh calamansi juice (substitute Sun Tropics brand if fresh isn’t available)
method: Dry shake all ingredients (except bitters) until frothy. Add 8 small ice cubes and shake vigorously. Double strain into a large coupe and top with bitters. Garnish with an edible flower.
storyTitle: Summertime Sippers

name: Rye and Thyme
ingredients: 1 1/4 oz. Fort Hamilton Double Barrel rye (or other rye)
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake until well chilled, about 15 seconds. Double strain into a chilled coupe and garnish with thyme sprig.

subs.name: Thyme Honey
subs.method: Combine honey and water in a pot over low heat and bring to a simmer. Stir until well combined, about 5 to 10 minutes. Add thyme sprigs and remove from heat. Once cool, strain into an airtight container. Keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.

storyTitle: This Culinary Cocktail Is Perfect for Summer Entertaining

name: Cherry & Fennel Salad
credit: Serves 4
ingredients: 1 lb. fresh pitted red cherries (sweet or sour)
2 heads fennel, shaved thin 2 bunches arugula
3/4 cup walnuts, toasted and salted (or candied)
1/3 cup extra virgin olive oil Sea salt to taste
2 oz. Briar Rose Fata Morgana cheese (or other high-quality feta)
method: With a torch or your oven’s broiler, roast the pitted cherries quickly to soften them while giving a slight singe, about 2 minutes. Place the toasted cherries and their juices into a small mixing bowl with the red wine vinegar, minced shallot, and black pepper. Toss to coat. Set aside to marinate for about 20 minutes. In a separate medium mixing bowl, combine thinly shaved fennel, arugula, and toasted walnuts. Strain out half of the cherries from the vinegar mixture and reserve. Place the remaining vinegar mixture in a blender and blend on low to puree the cherries. Slowly add the olive oil and sea salt. Combine the cherry-black pepper vinaigrette with. the salad mixture and gently toss. Finish by topping with cheese crumbles and the remaining marinated cherries.
storyTitle: Pair These Whiskey Cocktails With This Summer Salad

name: Cherry Smash
credit: Serves 1
intro: This cocktail “complements the salad by highlighting the cherry and spice,” explains Uniss. That, in turn, “accentuates cherry notes in the Old Forester bourbon.”
ingredients: 2 oz. Old Forester Statesman (or other bourbon)
Place cherries in a rocks glass and splash with bitters. Muddle the cherries until mostly smashed.
method: Fill a cocktail shaker with ice, add bourbon, vermouth, simple syrup, and lemon juice. Cover and shake vigorously, then strain over the cherries and fresh ice. Garnish with a whole cherry.
storyTitle: Pair These Whiskey Cocktails With This Summer Salad

name: Mountain Mint Julep
credit: Serves 1
intro: Unlike the Smash, this cocktail serves as a contrast to the flavors on the plate. It's a "bright and refreshing departure from the fruit and spice notes of the salad," Uniss explains, "acting as a bit of a palate cleanser by leaning on the herbaceous notes in the whiskey and mint."
method: In a Julep cup or Highball glass, lightly muddle two mint sprigs in the simple syrup. Add the bourbon and then pack the cup or glass tightly with crushed ice. Stir until the vessel is frosted on the outside. Top with more crushed ice to form an ice cone on top, and garnish with a sprig of mint and a dash of bitters.
storyTitle: Pair These Whiskey Cocktails With This Summer Salad

name: The Happy Herbie
ingredients: 2 oz. Frank August Small Batch bourbon (or other high-rye bourbon)
1/2 oz. Greenbar Distillery Fruitlab jasmine liqueur
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin. Dry shake for 8 to 10 seconds. Add ice and shake again to chill, about 8 to 10 seconds. Strain into a coupe, express orange peel over top, then drop the peel into the drink or garnish on a pick.
storyTitle: A Whiskey Cocktail Perfect For Independence Day

name: Peach Julep
ingredients: 2 oz. Angels Envy (or other port-finished bourbon)
1 1/4 oz. housemade peach simple syrup (recipe below)
method: In a shaker tin, muddle mint leaves and lemon juice. Add remaining ingredients and ice, and shake for about 20 seconds. Strain over crushed ice in a rocks glass and garnish with mint sprigs.

subs.name: Housemade Peach Simple Syrup
ingredients: 3/4 cup white peach puree (such as Perfect Puree), thawed
subs.method: Bring water to a boil in a pot over high heat. Turn off heat, add sugar, and stir to dissolve. Once combined, cool completely (about 30 minutes). Add thawed peach puree. Transfer to a sealable container and keep refrigerated up to 7 days.

storyTitle: Celebrate Bourbon In Summertime With This Peachy Mint Julep

name: Smoke 'Em if You've Got 'Em
credit: Natalie Bovis
ingredients: 1 1/2 oz. Charles Goodnight bourbon (or other bourbon)
method: Set fire to the sprig of sage and cover it with a martini glass, allowing it to capture the smoke as the sprig burns. Pour all ingredients into a cocktail shaker and add ice. Shake and strain it into the glass. Garnish with fresh unburned sage leaves.
storyTitle: A Whisky Lover's Guide To Ancho Reyes Liqueur

name: Sassy Summer Sidecar
credit: Rocco DiLillo, bar manager at Albert's Bar in New York City
ingredients: 1 3/4 oz. Elijah Craig bourbon (or other bourbon)
method: Add all ingredients in a shake with ice. Shake and double strain into a salt-rimmed coupe. Garnish with lime wedge.
storyTitle: A Whisky Lover's Guide To Ancho Reyes Liqueur

name: FiReD uP Old Fashioned
credit: Mike Vacheresse, owner and head bartender at Travel Bar in Brooklyn
ingredients: 1 1/2 oz. Elijah Craig 12 year old Barrel Proof bourbon (or other barrel proof bourbon)
1 oz. Rothman & Winter orchard cherry liqueur
4 dashes Bittermens Hellfire habanero shrub bitters
method: Mix all ingredients and serve in a rocks glass over a large ice cube. Garnish with Luxardo cherries.
storyTitle: A Whisky Lover's Guide To Ancho Reyes Liqueur

name: Embers
credit: Stanislav Harcinik, bar ambassador at Mirror Bar in Bratislava, Slovakia
ingredients: 3 oz. The London Essence Co. roasted pineapple soda
method: Build the cocktail in a highball glass. Garnish with a roasted pineapple wedge and chile oil.
storyTitle: A Whisky Lover's Guide To Ancho Reyes Liqueur

name: Six Paths
ingredients: 4 dashes The Bitter Truth celery bitters
method: Combine whiskey, vermouths, bitters, and one sage leaf in a mixing glass. Lightly muddle. Add ice and stir until chilled, about 30 times. Rinse a chilled Nick and Nora glass with sage tincture. Double-strain cocktail into the prepared glass and garnish with remaining sage leaf.

subs.name: Sage Tincture
subs.method: In a nonreactive container, combine sage and Everclear. Let steep 24 hours. Fine strain into a sealable container. Store at room temperature for up to 30 days.

storyTitle: Sage Adds A Spring to This Perfect Manhattan’s Step

name: Peachy Quien
credit: Created by Ziv Scherman, food and beverage director, Blue Jay Bistro, Littleton, North Carolina
intro: This bright, lively drink starts with sweet peach, then the heat starts to build. Scherman recommends serving it with a burger, ideally one topped with bacon, cheddar, and tangy barbecue sauce.
ingredients: 1½ oz. Stranahan’s Original (or other smoky American single malt)
½ oz. jalapeño simple syrup (recipe below)
Smoked chardonnay salt and jalapeño slice for garnish

Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake about 10 seconds to chill. Rim a rocks glass with salt. Place a large ice cube in the glass. Strain cocktail over ice and garnish with jalapeño slice.
method: Place all ingredients in a metal or hard plastic bowl and refrigerate for 4 hours to steep. Remove peaches and purée in a blender until smooth. Transfer to a sealable container and keep refrigerated for up to 3 days. Strain remaining jalapeño syrup into a sealable container. Keep refrigerated for up to 1 week.
storyTitle: Make These Whiskey Cocktails Created for Grilling Season

name: Pistachio Paper Plane
credit: Created by Chris Chernock, beverage director, Asterid, Los Angeles
intro: “The subtle sweet notes of summer peach and bourbon in this cocktail help to balance out the warm charred notes of grilled chicken wings, while the citrus cleanses the palate between bites,” Chernock says.
ingredients: ¾ oz. Matchbook Distilling Co. Day Trip Peach amaro
¾ oz. toasted pistachio-infused bourbon (recipe below)
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake vigorously for 20 to 25 seconds. Double strain into a Nick and Nora or coupe. Preheat oven to 450° F. Spread pistachios evenly on a baking sheet and roast until fragrant and brownish, about 10 to 12 minutes. Remove from oven. While still warm, use a muddler or mallet to break pistachios into pieces. Place pieces in a vessel with bourbon; cover and let sit at room temperature for 24 hours. Fine-strain through cheesecloth into a sealable container. Keep refrigerated for up to 1 month.
storyTitle: Make These Whiskey Cocktails Created for Grilling Season

name: Ruby Rush
credit: Created by Rebecca Mullis, bar administrator, Husk Savannah
intro: This silky, subtly sweet play on the Gold Rush pairs well with grilled fish. “The brightness of the lemon and hibiscus, plus the rye, which is lower-ABV, won’t be overpowered by a lighter protein,” Mullis explains.
ingredients: 2 oz. Catoctin Creek Roundstone rye 80 proof (or other low-proof rye)
Lemon wheel and edible flower for garnish
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake 15 to 20 seconds. Strain into a rocks glass over a large cube. Garnish with lemon wheel and edible flower. Combine all ingredients in a saucepan over low heat. Bring to a simmer and cook 10 minutes. Remove from heat to cool, then strain into a sealable container. Keep refrigerated for up to 1 month.
storyTitle: Make These Whiskey Cocktails Created for Grilling Season

name: Summer Smash
credit: Created by Reece Morris, manager and bartender, Dapper Duck, Orlando
intro: “The oakiness of the Irish whiskey comes through the sweet strawberry lemonade, making this a good pairing with smoked barbecue ribs,” Morris says.
ingredients: 1½ oz. Proper No. 12 (or other Irish single malt)
Lemon wheel and mint sprig for garnish
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for 5 seconds. Fine-strain into a Collins glass filled with ice. Garnish with lemon wheel and mint sprig.
storyTitle: Make These Whiskey Cocktails Created for Grilling Season

name: The Bourbon Street
credit: Created by Shafique Sobers, bar manager, Skylark, New York City
intro: The sweeter notes in this tart, slightly smoky cocktail contrast with a savory burger, Sobers says.
ingredients: 1½ oz. Wyoming Whiskey Outryder (or rye whiskey)
¾ oz. black cherry-infused syrup (like Reàl Black Cherry Puree syrup)
3 brandied cherries and lemon wheel for garnish
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for 15 seconds, then double strain over ice in a rocks glass. Garnish with cherries on a toothpick and lemon wheel on top.
storyTitle: Make These Whiskey Cocktails Created for Grilling Season

name: Walking on Sunshine
credit: Created by Dee Ann Quinones, beverage consultant, DWD Designs, Los AngelesSt-Germain and lemon keep things bright, while ginger beer plays up bourbon’s spice in this refreshing drink.
ingredients: ¾ oz. Kin Brown bourbon (or other 80-proof bourbon)
method: Combine bourbon, St-Germain, lemon juice, and bitters in a wine goblet or Collins glass. Add ice cubes. Top with ginger beer and stir to incorporate. Garnish with pansy.
storyTitle: Don't Sacrifice Flavor With These Low-ABV Cocktails

name: Double Duty
credit: Created by Joel Lee Kulp, bar manager, The Richardson, BrooklynPimm’s No. 1 adds a sweet fruitiness to light blended scotch, and soda water and sparkling wine make this spritz super refreshing.
ingredients: 1 oz. Duncan Taylor Politician (or other light-bodied blended scotch)
Cucumber ribbon and orange twist for garnish
method: Add all ingredients except soda water and sparkling wine to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for 5-10 seconds. Strain into a Collins glass filled with fresh ice. Top with soda water and sparkling wine. Garnish with cucumber ribbon and orange twist. Combine water and salt in a jar and shake until salt is dissolved. Let cool, then transfer to a dropper bottle. Keep refrigerated for up to one month.
storyTitle: Don't Sacrifice Flavor With These Low-ABV Cocktails

name: Thistle Italy
credit: Created by Nick Farrell, spirits director, Show of Hands, Washington, D.C.This cocktail is a symphony of well-balanced flavors. “Cynar and strawberries go incredibly well together, and the salt cuts through a little of the amaro’s bitterness, while the peppercorn adds a touch of spice that mimics some of the heat lost from the whisky’s lower alcohol content,” Farrell says.
ingredients: ½ oz. Wilderness Trail Bottled in Bond rye (or other bonded rye whiskey)
½ oz. Cocchi Storico Vermouth di Torino
method: In a mixing glass, muddle strawberries, salt, pink peppercorns, and rye. Add ice and remaining ingredients. Stir for 20 seconds. Strain into a chilled coupe. Garnish with strawberry on the glass rim.
storyTitle: Don't Sacrifice Flavor With These Low-ABV Cocktails

name: Toki Iced Tea
credit: Created by Svetlana Altarrasy, head bartender, Casa Sensei, Fort Lauderdale“This drink is very light, refreshing, and a little fizzy. The mint and cardamom add a dimension of freshness and spice, balancing out the citrus and hints of vanilla and ginger from the whisky,” Altarrasy says.
ingredients: 1 oz. Suntory Toki (or other blended Japanese whisky)
Lemon wheel and large mint sprig for garnish
method: Add all ingredients except soda water to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for 5 to 7 seconds. Strain into a Collins glass filled with fresh ice and top with soda. Garnish with lemon wheel and mint sprig.
storyTitle: Don't Sacrifice Flavor With These Low-ABV Cocktails

name: Maestro
ingredients: 2 oz. Suntory Toki (or other blended Japanese whisky)
method: Add ice to a mixing glass, then add all ingredients. Stir for 35 seconds. Strain into a rocks glass over a large cube. Garnish with lemon peel.

subs.name: Morita Pepper Syrup
subs.method: Combine water and sugar in a pot, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Cook until sugar dissolves, about 2-3 minutes. Add peppers and allow to come to a boil again. After a few seconds, remove pot from heat. Let cool to room temperature, then strain into a sealable container. Keep refrigerated for up to 3 weeks.

storyTitle: Swap Your Margarita for This Spicy Cinco de Mayo Cocktail

name: Crimson and Clover
ingredients: 1 1/2 oz. Woodford Reserve (or other straight bourbon)
1/4 oz. raspberry puree (Sweeney recommends Perfect Puree)
Freeze-dried raspberry powder or fresh raspberries for garnish
method: Place all ingredients in a shaker tin. Shake vigorously to integrate the egg white with the other ingredients, about 5 to 7 seconds. Add about 8 ice cubes and shake for another 8 to 10 seconds. Strain into a coupe and let sit for 25 to 30 seconds to allow the foam to line the top of the drink. Dust raspberry powder on top or garnish with raspberries on a pick.
storyTitle: Whiskey and Wine Make a Gorgeous Cocktail

name: Toasted Pecan Sable Cookie
ingredients: 1 cup plus 1 Tbsp. pecans, whole or pieces
⅓ cup plus 2 Tbsp. oat flour
storyTitle: Pecan Sable & Malted Milk Whiskey Chocolate Ganache Cookies

name: Whipped Malted Milk Chocolate Whiskey Ganache
ingredients: 7 oz. high-quality milk chocolate, roughly chopped
method: Place the chocolate in a double broiler over medium heat. Stir occasionally until completely melted. Whisk together heavy cream, whiskey, salt, and malted milk powder in a small pot. Place over medium-low heat. When the cream is hot and steam is visibly rising from the pot, remove from heat and pour over the melted chocolate. With a rubber spatula, stir the cream and chocolate from the middle working outward until glossy and smooth. Pour into a sealed container and chill for at least 1 hour. With an electric mixer fitted with the whisk attachment, whip on high for 5 minutes, or until pale in color and doubled in volume.
storyTitle: Pecan Sable & Malted Milk Whiskey Chocolate Ganache Cookies

name: Between Living And Dreaming
credit: Nikki McCutcheon, senior director of beverage for New York City-based Tao Group Hospitality
ingredients: 2 oz. Suntory Toki blended Japanese whisky
2 dashes The Japanese Bitters Co. Sakura bitters
method: Combine all ingredients in a rocks glass. Add a large ice cube, stir, and garnish with an orange peel, expressing the peel over the drink first.
storyTitle: The Old Fashioned Reimagined

name: Cereal Killer
credit: Nikki McCutcheon, senior director of beverage for New York City-based Tao Group Hospitality
ingredients: 1 1/2 oz. Apple Jacks-infused Maker’s Mark (recipe below)
3 dashes Hella Cocktail Co. apple blossom bitters
method: Stir all ingredients with ice in a mixing glass for approximately 30 revolutions. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube, and garnish with an orange peel, expressing the peel over the drink first.
storyTitle: The Old Fashioned Reimagined

name: 1929 - Cubism Old Fashioned
credit: Sarah Kornegay, bartender at The Katherine Brasserie & Bar in Winston-Salem, North Carolina
method: Add orange juice, syrup, cherry, and bitters in a large ice mold. Fill the ice mold the rest of the way with water and freeze. Once frozen, place cube in a rocks glass and pour bourbon over it. Garnish with an orange peel, expressing the peel over the drink first.
storyTitle: The Old Fashioned Reimagined

name: Chamomile Fields
credit: John Ware, bar director at Forsythia in New York City
ingredients: 1/2 oz. Gualco Camomilla grappa-based chamomile liqueur
method: Combine all ingredients in a rocks glass. Add a large ice cube, stir briefly, and garnish with a lemon peel, expressing the peel over the drink first.
storyTitle: The Old Fashioned Reimagined

name: Fall Old Fashioned
credit: Mike Liay, director of beverage for Minneapolis-based Jester Concepts
method: Stir all ingredients with ice in a mixing glass. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube, and garnish with an orange peel, expressing the peel over the drink first.
storyTitle: The Old Fashioned Reimagined

name: Bohemian Raspberry
ingredients: 2 oz. Buffalo Trace (or other wheated bourbon)
3 raspberries and 1 mint sprig for garnish
method: In a mixing glass, add bourbon raspberry syrup, lime juice, and mint leaves. Fill the glass 3/4 full with cubed ice. Cap your mixing glass with a shaker tin and shake for 15 to 20 seconds. Add ginger beer. Fill a Collins glass 3/4 full with cubed ice. Strain the cocktail over the ice. Garnish with raspberries on a pick and spanked mint sprig.

subs.name: Raspberry Simple Syrup
subs.method: Place sugar and raspberries in a stainless-steel pot. Muddle until a thick paste forms. Add water and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring continuously. Remove from heat and strain into a sealable container. Allow to cool. Cover and refrigerate for up to five days.

storyTitle: Spring Into Warmer Days With the Bohemian Raspberry

name: Almond Tart Crust
ingredients: ½ cup unsalted butter, cold, cubed.
method: Freeze bourbon for at least 24 hours. Preheat oven to 350º F. Whisk together dry ingredients in a medium bowl. Add cold cubed butter and press the flour with your hands or a pastry cutter until a cohesive dough forms. Add the egg yolks and the cold bourbon. Mix until just combined and the dough is moist, with no dry bits remaining. Dump onto a clean flat work surface and knead 3-4 times until cohesive and slightly sticky. Press the dough evenly into a 9” tart or pie dish using the back of a measuring cup. Prick the bottom and sides of the dough all over with a fork. Freeze for at least 30 minutes and up to one hour. Bake the tart shell for 15 minutes until firm and slightly golden. Let cool while you prepare the custard filling.
storyTitle: Make This Bourbon and Meyer Lemon Flip Tart

name: Custard filling
ingredients: 3 Tbsp. Meyer lemon zest, grated, from roughly five Meyer lemons
method: Preheat oven to 325º F. Combine all ingredients in a large bowl or a standing mixer fitted with the whisk attachment. Whisk until thoroughly combined and homogenous. Pour mixture into slightly cooled tart shell. Tightly cover the filled tart with tin foil. Bake for 25-30 until the custard is set. Remove from the oven and cool completely. Chill in the refrigerator.
storyTitle: Make This Bourbon and Meyer Lemon Flip Tart

name: Ginger Mascarpone Whipped Cream
method: Whisk together the heavy cream and ginger root. Heat in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming. Remove from heat, cover, and let sit for 30 minutes. Strain cream through a sieve into a clean container to remove the ginger, seal tightly, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight. Discard ginger. Once chilled, whip the cream and powdered sugar with a standing mixer or a whisk until soft peaks form and slightly hold their shape. Set aside. Whip mascarpone with an electric or stand mixer with a paddle attachment on high for 2-3 minutes until smooth and aerated. Gently fold together the mascarpone and ginger whipped cream. Dollop onto the chilled tart and serve immediately. Refrigerate, tightly covered, for up to three days.
storyTitle: Make This Bourbon and Meyer Lemon Flip Tart

name: Amai Shio
ingredients: 1 1/4 oz. Suntory Toki (or other Japanese whisky)
method: Rim half a rocks glass with togarashi seasoning. Add remaining ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Hard shake 15 seconds. Strain over a large cube in prepared rocks glass.

subs.name: Rosemary Tangerine Cordial
subs.method: Combine all ingredients in a pot over medium heat and bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Let cool, then double strain into cocktail shaker. Yields 1 serving.

storyTitle: Sweet, Salty, Spicy—This Cocktail Has It All

name: Apple Drop
ingredients: 1 1/2 oz. Bushmills Original (or other blended Irish)
method: In a shaker tin, combine all ingredients except bitters. Fill the shaker with ice cubes. Vigorously shake for 10 to 15 seconds. Strain into a coupe. Add bitters on top. Place apple slices on the rim of the glass or float them on the surface of the cocktail as a garnish.
storyTitle: Make An Apple Drop Irish Whiskey Cocktail This St. Patrick's Day

name: Old Ireland
ingredients: 2 oz. Bushmills Black Bush (or other sherry cask-finished Irish whiskey)
method: Fill a mixing glass with ice. Add whiskey, syrup, both bitters, and saline. Stir 15 to 20 seconds. Strain over a large ice cube in a rocks glass. Hold orange peel over the drink and express the oils over top.

subs.name: Guinness Demerara Syrup
subs.method: Combine Guinness and both sugars in a saucepan. Heat over low heat, stirring continuously, until the sugar dissolves and mixture thickens, about 15 to 20  minutes. Remove from heat and let cool. Then strain into an airtight container. Keep refrigerated for up to two weeks.

storyTitle: Make This Old Fashioned With An Irish Twist

name: Descent Into Averna
ingredients: 2 oz. WhistlePig 6 year old PiggyBack rye (or other rye)
2 dashes Fee Brothers Black Walnut bitters
method: Rinse a coupe glass with absinthe. Combine remaining ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir until chilled, about 40 to 60 revolutions. Strain into prepared coupe and garnish with star anise.
storyTitle: A Dimensional Cocktail That's Easy to Enjoy

name: Spinach Fettuccine and Smoked Salmon, Asparagus, and Cream
credit: Serves 6 as an appetizer; 4 as an entreeGetty Images
method: Season asparagus with salt and pepper. Over medium heat, saute asparagus in butter for 2 minutes. Add chopped shallots and cook until softened. Add cream, turn heat to medium-high, and boil until mixture is slightly reduced. Cook fettuccine in salted boiling water according to package and drain. Add chunks of bite-size pieces of salmon to cream, toss with pasta, and serve immediately
storyTitle: Burns Night Dinner Recipes With a Modern Twist

name: Whisky Ribeye
credit: Serves 4
method: Heat a cast iron skillet on high heat for 10 minutes. Season the steaks liberally with salt and pepper and add the steaks to the dry skillet. Sear the steaks for about 4 minutes on each side. When all of the steaks have a nice crust, add butter and thyme to the pan. Once the butter is incorporated into all of the juices, turn off the burner. Deglaze the pan with the whiskey. Plate each steak with the Sicilian spinach (recipe below) and pour some of the whisky butter on each steak.
storyTitle: Burns Night Dinner Recipes With a Modern Twist

name: Sicilian Spinach
credit: Serves 4
method: Cover sultanas in warm water and soak for a few minutes. Add the butter to a pan over medium heat. Saute pine nuts in the butter to toast, then add garlic and drained raisins. Quickly wilt the spinach in the pan and season with salt and pepper.
storyTitle: Burns Night Dinner Recipes With a Modern Twist

name: Apple Cranberry Streusel Tart
credit: Serves 6
intro: Getty ImagesEasy Tart Shell Crust
method: Mix flour, granulated sugar, powdered sugar, and salt in a bowl. Set aside. Melt the butter. Make a well in the dry ingredients and pour butter in the middle. Stir together until dough forms, adding a bit of water if needed. While still warm press the dough into a 9-inch tart or pie pan. Spread evenly and work out to the edges to form a shell. Refrigerate.

subs.name: Apple-Cranberry Filling
subs.method: Add all ingredients to a bowl. Stir. Set aside.

subs.name: Streusel Topping
ingredients: ¼ lb. butter, cut into small cubes
subs.method: Add all ingredients to a bowl. Using your hands, mix all ingredients together and work until butter is crumbly. Preheat oven to 350° F. Remove tart shell from refrigerator and pour in filling. Evenly top with streusel. Bake for 30 to 40 minutes, or until desired color is reached. Let it cool and serve at room temperature, topped with a scoop of vanilla or salted caramel ice cream.

storyTitle: Burns Night Dinner Recipes With a Modern Twist

name: Chocolate-Washed Sazerac
ingredients: Orange zest and absinthe (optional) for garnish
method: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice. Stir for 1 minute. Strain over a large rock in a rocks glass. Garnish with orange zest. If desired, spray glass with absinthe for a final anise-forward touch.

subs.name: Cocoa Rye
ingredients: 1 bottle (750 ml) Pikesville Rye (or other rye)
subs.method: Heat butter in a saucepot over low heat until melted. Add cocoa nibs, mix well, and cook for about 5 minutes. Turn heat off. Add whisky and let rest for 2 hours. Cover and refrigerate for 2 days, then strain over a coffee filter into the whisky bottle or other sealed container. Whisky keeps indefinitely and is shelf-stable.

storyTitle: Chocolate and Whiskey Make the Ideal Valentine's Day Cocktail

name: Sin On Wheels
credit: Ron Dillon, assistant general manager at Adalina in Chicago
method: Muddle cherries in the bottom of a 100-proof cherries cocktail shaker with bourbon, syrup, vermouth, bourbon cherry juice, and bitters. Add ice and shake. syrup Strain into a coupe and garnish with a cocktail cherry and an orange peel.
storyTitle: Cocktail Cherries Go Beyond Garnishing

name: Out With The Old Fashioned
credit: Sara Bradley, chef and proprietor of Freight House in Paducah, Kentucky
ingredients: 4 dashes The Bitter Truth Orange bitters
method: In a rocks glass, add syrup, lemon slice, and bitters. Gently muddle the lemon slice, focusing on the flesh of the lemon, not the rind. Add the cherry and smash once. Place a large ice cube in the glass and add whiskey. Stir 25-30 times.
storyTitle: Cocktail Cherries Go Beyond Garnishing

name: The Bullfighter
credit: Mark Gallagher, bartender at Talbott Cucina in Chicago
method: In a glass heatproof mug, muddle five cocktail cherries and marmalade. Add hot water and stir to melt the marmalade. Add scotch and liqueur and stir again. Garnish with remaining cherries on a cocktail pick.
storyTitle: Cocktail Cherries Go Beyond Garnishing

name: Cherry Bread Pudding
credit: Serves 6-8
ingredients: 12 day-old doughnuts (glazed or plain) or bread of your choice (brioche or croissants are ideal)
1 1/2 tsp. ground cinnamon Ice cream of your choice, optional
method: • Preheat oven to 325° F.• Cut doughnuts or bread into small pieces (1/2" x 1/2"), add to a large mixing bowl, and set aside.• Simmer dried cherries in water for 5 minutes, drain, and toss in a bowl with 1 Tbsp. sugar and 1 1/2 tsp. cinnamon, or to taste. Set aside.• Blend heavy cream, milk, 1/2 cup sugar, eggs, vanilla, and salt in a blender for 45-60 seconds. Pour over the doughnut pieces and mix together.• Place half of the mixture into a greased 9"x13" pan. Add cherries, followed by the remaining bread pudding mixture. Cover with aluminum foil and place into a larger pan that has approximately 1-2" of water in it. It should reach halfway up the sides of the 9"x13" pan.• Bake for 40-50 minutes, covered. Check for doneness by pulling back the foil and inserting a toothpick into the center to make sure there is no longer any liquid when it’s removed.• Serve warm, along with a scoop of your favorite ice cream. AARON CONWAY
storyTitle: The Proof is in This Cherry Bread Pudding

name: Man of the Woods
credit: Serves 1
ingredients: 3 dashes Bittercube Cherry Bark Vanilla bitters
1 drop spruce or birch extract and lemon wheel for garnish
method: Combine all ingredients with ice in a mixing glass and stir until chilled. Double strain into a coupe and garnish with a single drop of birch or spruce extract and lemon wheel.
storyTitle: The Proof is in This Cherry Bread Pudding

name: Three Knuckle Formula
credit: Created by Steveie Smith, operations manager, Devil May Care, Austin“This Whiskey Sour riff packs a lot of complexity for having just four ingredients,” Smith says. “Earthy turmeric provides a counterfoil to the brighter, more aromatic flavors in the drink, leading the drinker to keep returning so they can further parse its layers of flavor.”
ingredients: 1½ oz. St. George Baller (or other fruit-forward American single malt)
Candied apricots on a pick for garnish
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for 10 seconds. Strain into a coupe and garnish with candied apricots.Turmeric Orgeat Stir ingredients in a bowl until well mixed. Transfer back into the orgeat syrup container. Keep refrigerated for up to 60 days.
storyTitle: Spice Up Your Whisky Cocktails With Seasonings

name: The Dancing Pig
credit: Created by Michelle LaBorde, sommelier and lead bartender, Dancing Bear Appalachian Bistro, Townsend, Tennessee“This cocktail delivers sweet and savory flavors perfect for whiskey lovers looking for something extra,” LaBorde says. “The smokiness of the bitters and the bacon syrup are a perfect match to the barrel aging of the bourbon.”
ingredients: ¾ oz. bacon pepper brown sugar syrup (recipe below)
1 rolled candied bacon strip for garnish
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice. Shake for 12 seconds. Strain into a rocks glass over a fresh cube and garnish with candied bacon. Combine all ingredients in a saucepan over high heat until lightly boiling. Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes. Strain through cheesecloth into a sealable container. Keep refrigerated for up to 1 week.
storyTitle: Spice Up Your Whisky Cocktails With Seasonings

name: Lucky Dragon
credit: Created by Henry Dwyer, bar manager, Hutong New York, New York CitySmooth, smoky, rich, and elegant, this makes an impressive cocktail for hosting guests, Dwyer says.
ingredients: ½ oz. Ancho Reyes verde chile poblano liqueur
method: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir 20 times. Strain into a cocktail glass and garnish with lemon twist. Combine five-spice powder and Everclear in a nonreactive container. Allow to sit for no more than 4 hours. Strain into an airtight container. Will keep indefinitely at room temperature.
storyTitle: Spice Up Your Whisky Cocktails With Seasonings

name: Persephone’s Kiss
credit: Created by Anne Hester, bar manager, Southernside Brewing Co., Greenville, South Carolina“This cocktail has rich, fruity flavors with a ginger kick that highlights the subtle flavor of licorice and pairs beautifully with the whisky,” Hester says.
ingredients: 1½ oz. Jameson Black Barrel (or other Irish whiskey)
1 oz. pomegranate star anise syrup (recipe below)
Dehydrated lime wheel and star anise for garnish
method: Add whiskey, syrup, lime juice, and ginger bitters to a shaker tin. Fill with ice and shake hard for at least 10 seconds. Strain into an ice-filled Collins glass. Top with ginger beer, then garnish with dehydrated lime wheel and star anise. Place star anise in a medium pot and warm over medium-low heat until fragrant, about 5 minutes, making sure it doesn’t burn. Meanwhile, combine sugar, water, and pomegranate juice in a bowl. Once the star anise is fragrant, add the mixture to the pot and simmer on low until the sugar is dissolved, about 3-5 minutes. Add pomegranate seeds and simmer for 10 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool before straining into a sealable container. Keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.
storyTitle: Spice Up Your Whisky Cocktails With Seasonings

name: Wood Smoke
ingredients: 1 3/4 oz. Johnnie Walker Black Label (or any smoky blended scotch)
1/2 oz. candy cap mushroom-infused maple syrup (recipe below)
2 dashes Ms. Better's Cypress Bowl bitters
method: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with ice and stir 15 seconds. Strain into a chilled rocks glass over a large block of ice. Garnish with lemon peel.

subs.name: Candy Cap Mushroom-Infused Maple Syrup
subs.method: Add syrup to boiling water and stir to combine well. Add mushrooms and allow to cool to room temperature. Strain into a bottle. Keep refrigerated for 2 weeks.

storyTitle: This Drink Tastes Like a Walk in the Woods

name: Rye and Chai Toddy
ingredients: Lemon wheel and cinnamon stick, for garnish
method: Add honey-oat syrup, bitters, and lemon juice to a mug and stir well to integrate. Pour in whiskey, brandy, and tea, and stir to combine. Garnish with lemon wheel and cinnamon stickHoney Oat Syrup Combine oats, cinnamon, and honey in a glass jar and seal. Let sit for 3 to 4 days. Add water, mix thoroughly, then strain into an airtight container. Keep refrigerated for 4 to 5 weeks.
storyTitle: Take the Chill Off With This Hot Toddy Twist

name: Gingerbread Sour
credit: Created by Jorge Centeno, chief spirits officer, Deer Path Inn, Lake Forest, IllinoisA scotch rinse lends an alluring peaty aroma and flavor to this refreshing velvety cocktail that’s filled with warm baking spices.
ingredients: ¼ oz. Ardbeg 10 year old (or other peated single malt scotch)
2 oz. Elijah Craig rye (or other rye)
½ oz. aquafaba or egg white
method: Rinse a coupe with scotch. Add rye, lemon juice, orange juice, gingerbread syrup, and aquafaba to a shaker tin. Dry shake for 15 seconds. Add ice and shake vigorously for 15 seconds. Double strain into the prepared coupe and dust with cinnamon.Gingerbread Syrup Add all ingredients except honey to a saucepan. Stir slowly over low heat until sugar is dissolved, about 15 minutes. Increase heat to medium and bring to a boil, then immediately reduce heat to low and simmer 5 minutes. Remove from heat, strain into a mason jar, and add honey, stirring slowly until it dissolves (about 1-2 minutes). Seal and keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.
storyTitle: Make Mine A Double: Cocktails That Mix Two Styles of Whisky

name: The Outlander
credit: Created by Michael Nathan, bar manager, Aphotic, San FranciscoThis cocktail is “a robust blend of fruits and baking spice, encapsulating the comforting warmth of a winter evening,” Nathan claims.
ingredients: 1 oz. Dad’s Hat bottled in bond (or other bonded rye)
½ oz. Highland Park 12 year old (or other mildly peated single malt scotch)
½ oz. Pierre Ferrand dry curaçao
method: Add all ingredients to a large mixing tin and fill with ice. Stir for roughly 15 seconds, until mixing glass is chilled to the touch. Strain into a coupe and serve. Pineapple Syrup 1¼ cups pineapple juice 1¼ cups white sugar½ tsp. citric acid powder In a blender, combine all ingredients until sugar is dissolved and mixture is uniform. Strain into an airtight container. Keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.
storyTitle: Make Mine A Double: Cocktails That Mix Two Styles of Whisky

name: Black Walnut Manhattan
credit: Created by Nate Wilson, lead bartender, AVOW Napa, Napa, CaliforniaThis sophisticated and mysterious Manhattan has a smooth and edgy flavor that transitions to a well-balanced nutty finish, Wilson says.
ingredients: ½ oz. Gryphon & Grain California bourbon (or other wheated bourbon)
3 dashes Fee Brothers Black Walnut bitters
Brandied cherry and candied walnut for garnish
method: Add all ingredients to a large mixing tin and fill with ice. Stir for 15-20 seconds. Strain into a Nick and Nora glass. Garnish with brandied cherry and candied walnut.
storyTitle: Make Mine A Double: Cocktails That Mix Two Styles of Whisky

name: Buenos Mate
credit: Created by Megan Luedtke, bar director, DDP Restaurant Group, Minneapolis“This is the perfect winter drink when you’re craving something mouthwatering and effervescent,” Luedtke says. While light and refreshing, it’s also layered with notes of herbs, acidity, and warm spices.
ingredients: 1½ oz. Keeper’s Heart Irish & American (or other Irish or rye whiskey)
½ oz. yerba mate honey syrup (recipe below)
method: Assemble all ingredients in a mixing glass or tin. Pour into a Collins glass over ice shards. Garnish with a yerba mate leaf.

subs.name: Yerba Mate Honey Syrup
subs.method: In a cup, combine water and tea and let steep for 15 minutes. Strain into mixing glass. Add remaining ingredients and stir well to combine. Transfer to a sealed container and keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.

storyTitle: Make Mine A Double: Cocktails That Mix Two Styles of Whisky

name: Osouji Fizz
ingredients: 2 oz. Suntory Toki (or other Japanese whisky)
2 oz. dry sparkling wine (preferably a brut champagne)
method: Add all ingredients except champagne to a shaker tin and shake without ice for 15 seconds. Add ice and shake for another 15 seconds. Add 1 oz. sparkling wine to a chilled 10-oz. Collins glass. Strain cocktail into glass. Top with remaining 1 oz. sparkling wine.

subs.name: Vanilla Hojicha Syrup
subs.method: Combine all ingredients in a pot over medium heat and bring to a boil. Once it comes to a boil, remove from heat, and let sit for one hour. Once cool to room temperature, strain into a plastic or non-reactive container. Keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.

storyTitle: Ring in the New Year With This Whisky Cocktail

credit: From the bar at Deviation Distilling in Denver
ingredients: ¼ oz. maple-infused syrup (equal parts maple syrup and warm water)
method: Pour fat-washed bourbon, syrup, and bitters into a mixing glass filled with ice. Stir to chill and strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube. Garnish with orange peel.
storyTitle: Fat-Washed Whisky Cocktails

name: The Upside Down
credit: From Empress by Boon in San Francisco
ingredients: 1 oz. sesame-washed Suntory Toki (or other Japanese whisky)*
¾ oz. Polugar No. 2 Garlic and Pepper vodka
4 drops The Japanese Bitters Umami bitters
method: *2oz. of sesameoilto750mlofwhiskyisrecommended Combine fat-washed whisky, vodka, syrup, lime juice, and bitters in a mixing tin. Shake and double strain into a Collins glass. Remove from heat and let cool for 20 minutes. Strain into a sealable container. Store in refrigerator up to 5 days.
storyTitle: Fat-Washed Whisky Cocktails

name: Los Isleños
credit: From Corrida in Boulder
ingredients: 2 oz. A5 Wagyu beef fat-washed Jura 10 year old (or other Island scotch)*
¼ oz. Bigallet China China Amer liqueur
¼ oz. Hateruma Island sugar syrup (see below)

storyTitle: Fat-Washed Whisky Cocktails

name: Standing Ovation
credit: From The Roosevelt Room in Austin

storyTitle: Fat-Washed Whisky Cocktails

name: Tequila Old Fashioned
ingredients: 1 1/4 oz. Wild Turkey 101 (or other high-rye bourbon)
3/4 oz. Patron añejo (or other añejo tequila)
Lemon twist and cherry for garnish
method: Add all ingredients to a mixing glass with one large ice cube and stir about 20 to 30 seconds. Brush the rim of an Old Fashioned glass with lemon twist. Strain drink into glass and garnish with cherry and lemon twist.
storyTitle: A Whisky and Tequila Cocktail for the Holidays

name: Fat-Washed Browned Butter Almond Cake with Bourbon Vanilla Buttercream Frosting
ingredients: 1/2 cup solidified bourbon-infused brown butter reserved from the fat wash recipe, room temperature
method: 1. At least 24 hours in advance, prepare brown butter-washed bourbon. Reserve the solidified fat that is removed after freezing and straining. 2. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees. Spray two 9-inch cake pans with non-stick oil. 3. Combine reserved solidified bourbon-infused browned butter, oil, and sugars in a bowl or a standing mixer fitted with the paddle attachment. Beat until fully incorporated. Set aside. 4. Whisk flours, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl until well combined. Set aside. 5. Add eggs one at a time to the butter and sugar mixture, scraping down the bowl as you go. 6. Add one-third of the flour mixture, beating on low. Turn the mixer off and add ⅓ of the whole milk. Scrape the bowl well and repeat in alternations until all the milk and flour mixture have been added and the batter is just combined. 7. Pour half the batter into each prepared pan. 8. Bake for 25-27 minutes until the cake bounces back when touched and a toothpick comes out clean. 9. Cool completely.

subs.name: Bourbon Soaking Syrup
subs.method: 1. Add sugar and water to a pot and bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring occasionally. 2. Remove from heat and stir in the fat-washed bourbon.

subs.name: Bourbon Vanilla Bean Buttercream
subs.method: 1. In a standing mixer with the paddle attachment or using a hand mixer, beat the butter on medium-high until whipped and pale in color, about 3 minutes. 2. Gradually add the sifted powdered sugar, beating on medium speed, scraping down the bowl after each addition. 3. Once all the sugar is added, beat on high for 2-3 minutes. 4. Add the fat-washed bourbon, vanilla paste, and salt and beat for another minute.

storyTitle: Fat-Washed Browned Butter Almond Cake with Bourbon Vanilla Bean Buttercream Frosting Recipe

name: Butter Kiss
credit: Created by Jason Marshall,  bar manager and beverage curator, The Ritz-Carlton, Portland, Ore.Inspired by black pepper butter corn and mashed sweet potatoes, this smooth, savory cocktail has a touch of smoke, spice, and a rich, creamy finish.
ingredients: 2 oz. Monkey Shoulder blended malt (or other blended scotch)
method: Add all ingredients to a shaker tin with ice and shake for 20 to 25 seconds. Double strain into a coupe glass and garnish with caramel corn.

subs.name: Butter Syrup
subs.method: Combine butter, sugar, milk, and honey in a saucepan over low to medium heat and gently bring to a boil. Immediately remove from heat and add baking soda. Stir slowly. Allow to cool, then transfer to an airtight container. Keep refrigerated for about one week.

storyTitle: The Perfect Whisky Cocktails to Serve With Thanksgiving Dinner

name: Señor Bond
credit: Created by Luis Villanueva, beverage director, Casa Bond, New York CitySpice notes from bourbon and bitters ensure this fall take on the Old Fashioned complements the herbs in your feast.
ingredients: 2 oz. Woodford Reserve (or other straight bourbon)
1/4 oz. Tippleman's Barrel Smoked maple syrup (or regular maple syrup)
Orange or lemon peel and amarena cherry for garnish
method: Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass with ice and stir for 60 seconds. Strain into a rocks glass and add a large ice cube. Garnish with citrus peel and cherry.
storyTitle: The Perfect Whisky Cocktails to Serve With Thanksgiving Dinner

name: Night Moves
credit: Created by Christian Taibi, executive bar czar, Mahina & Sun’s at The Surfjack Hotel & Swim Club, Waikiki, Hawaii“This warm, earthy digestif tells a story with every sip,” Taibi says. “Drinkers are greeted with a touch of brown sugar that gives off a nutty taste before getting a hint of minty cold.”
ingredients: 2 oz. Redemption Rye (or other rye whiskey)
2 dashes Fee Brothers Black Walnut bitters
Orange peel, mint leaf, and walnut for garnish
method: Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass. Add ice and stir for 20 rotations. Strain into double Old Fashioned glass over large ice cube. Express orange peel and discard. Garnish with mint leaf and/or walnut.

subs.name: Demerara Syrup
subs.method: Combine ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir until sugar is dissolved, about 10 minutes. Let cool, then transfer to a squeeze bottle. Keep refrigerated for up to two weeks.

storyTitle: The Perfect Whisky Cocktails to Serve With Thanksgiving Dinner

name: Fennely Honey! A Cocktail To Be Beary Passionate For
credit: Stephanie Reading, bar manager at Birdie G’s in Santa Monica, California
ingredients: 1 oz. Aberfeldy 12 year old single malt scotch
1/2 oz. orange blossom honey syrup (recipe below)
Dried fennel flowers or dehydrated lemon wheel for garnish
method: Lightly shake all ingredients in a Boston shaker with a few cubes of ice. Dump into a honey bear-shaped jar glass or other tall cocktail glass. Top with crushed ice and garnish with dried fennel flowers or a dehydrated lemon wheel.

Mint sprig and lemon peel for garnish
method: Stir all ingredients with ice in a mixing glass for 20-30 seconds. Strain into an ice-filled rocks glass and garnish with a mint sprig and lemon peel.

method: In an ice-filled Collins glass, add bourbon, Pimm's, and lime juice. Top with ginger beer and give a quick stir. Garnish with mint and strawberry.

method: Shake all ingredients with ice until the cocktail shaker is frosty. Strain through a mesh strainer into a Nick and Nora glass. Trim both ends of a strawberry Twizzlers to use as a straw.

method: Shake whiskey, Pimm's, lime juice, and honey with ice. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube. Top with a float of Guinness and garnish with an orange peel.

1/4 oz. Giffard Crème de Pêche peach liqueur

½ oz. J.F. Haden’s Espresso liqueur (or other espresso liqueur)
Dash cinnamon and orange peel, for garnish
method: In a mixing glass, muddle the sugar and orange wedges until the sugar is completely broken down (if using cubes). Fill the mixing glass with ice. Top with cinnamon and express an orange peel over the drink, then discard.

1/4 oz. Ardbeg 10 year old (or other peated scotch)

Sage leaves and dehydrated orange wheel for garnish
method: Muddle the fresh ginger in the bottom of a cocktail shaker until well-mashed. Add Glenmorangie, lavender honey syrup, and lemon juice, and fill shaker with ice. Shake until well chilled then double strain into a Highball glass. Top with ginger beer and pour the Ardbeg over the back of a bar spoon so that it floats atop the drink. Garnish with a few sage leaves and a dehydrated orange wheel.

2 dashes The Bitter Truth Grapefruit bitters
Candied grapefruit peel or grapefruit slice for garnish

name: Celebrate the 4th of July With These All-American Whiskey Cocktails
credit: Jacob Sunny, bartender at Bastille Brasserie and Bar in Alexandria, Virginia
intro: What better way to toast our country than with an ice-cold American whiskey cocktail? And with summer in full swing, there’s a bounty of fresh flavor-packed produce at our disposal, from stone fruits, berries, and melons to summertime herb staples basil and mint. All of these ingredients pair beautifully with America’s native spirit, be it bold and sweet bourbon, smooth Tennessee whiskey, spicy ry
ingredients: 1 oz. KO Bare Knuckle (or other cask strength bourbon)
method: Shake all ingredients vigorously with ice for 20 seconds and strain into a coupe. Express a lime peel over the cocktail then discard peel.The Season of The Witch Shake all ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled Collins glass.Pig’s Julep In a rocks glass, muddle the cucumber and mint. Add whiskey, liqueur, and syrup, plus crushed ice. Swizzle the drink and garnish with a mint sprig.Nashville Sour Shake all ingredients with ice and strain into an ice-filled Old Fashioned glass. Garnish with a lemon wheel and an edible flower. Strawberry-Infused Cocchi AmericanoIn a ½-gallon sealable container combine 400 grams (approximately 1 cup) thinly sliced strawberries and a 750 ml bottle Cocchi Americano. Seal and let infuse for a day or two in the fridge, then strain through a fine strainer lined with a coffee filter. Store refrigerated for up to 1 month. Rhubarb CordialPlace 600 grams (approximately 3 cups) sliced rhubarb in a food processor or blender and pulse to make a mash. Separately, in either a blender or on the stovetop, dissolve 3 cups sugar, 1 Tbsp. lemon in 5 cups water. Combine this solution and the mashed rhubarb in a container, cover, and let infuse overnight in the refrigerator. Strain through a fine strainer lined with a coffee filter. Store refrigerated for up to 6 weeks.
